video_title: Trevor Ariza gets HONEST about Dwight Howard and if he DESERVED to miss the NBA Top 75 👀

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard's work ethic and exclusion from NBA Top 75
quotes.excerpt: It surprised me that he wasn't part of Top 75.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Man, Trevor, you already know you played with the big fellow, Dwight Howard. I'm pretty sure you saw the work ethic. You saw him develop over the years. Tell me about him as a teammate and did it surprise you that he wasn't part of Top 75?

text_blocks.speaker: Trevor Ariza
text_blocks.text: It surprised me that he wasn't part of Top 75 player. He won three straight Defensive Player of the Year. He controlled the paint his whole healthy career, offensively and defensively. How many people have done that? Kareem, Shaq, who else? He controlled the paint like that.

quotes.speaker: Trevor Ariza
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard's intense work ethic and dedication to improvement
quotes.excerpt: He would be in the weight room lifting an hour and a half before practice.
quotes.quote: His work ethic was out of this world. He would be in the weight room lifting an hour and a half before practice. Then he would practice, then he would stay two, three, four hours after practice just shooting, working on the things that he wanted to work on to get better at. So, he is somebody that always worked on his game and just seeing that mentality and work ethic, you would think it should pay off with the accolades that come with it at the end of it. But yeah, he definitely should have been a Top 75 player.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Dwight Howard's personality and the criticism he received
quotes.excerpt: A lot of people criticize him for being just the he-he and ha-ha person.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: A lot of people criticize him for being just the he-he and ha-ha person. Do you think if he wasn't that he-he and ha-ha and been more on a different type of demeanor, like a Demarcus-type of attitude?

text_blocks.speaker: Trevor Ariza
text_blocks.text: Yeah, it would be different for him for sure. It would be no question what it is, but again, that's not his personality. In order to be his greatness, he has to be who he is, and that's what he was doing. So, I can't be mad at that.

quotes.speaker: Tony Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: The lack of veteran presence in today's NBA
quotes.excerpt: The turnover time is too fast.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Why don't you think the vets get the love like it used to be when the league was coming up? What do you think the difference is?

text_blocks.speaker: Trevor Ariza
text_blocks.text: The turnover time is too fast. To have an older guy, it messes up the younger person's opportunity in one space. But then it also keeps the young dudes young and their minds young too. Because if you think of it like when we were younger players, we had grown-ass men on our team with families who got kids the same age. It is just different now. The vets is 26, 25, 26. You are in a different mental space.

quotes.speaker: Trevor Ariza
quotes.summary_phrase: The value of veteran leadership for younger players
quotes.excerpt: I wish they would, though, because it would definitely help the younger players a lot more.
quotes.quote: I wish they would, though, because it would definitely help the younger players a lot more. If you just got somebody there helping them and teaching them more things, it would be better.
